section7_conclusion: The directive-required CAS contract holds on current HEAD. CAS atomicity, expected-value semantics, and updater visibility are correct; F-NEW-251's one-logical-slot invariant (interpreter field access, Unsafe, Atomic*FieldUpdater all address the same slot) needs no second field resolver and F-NEW-251 is NOT reopened.
section6_conclusion: ServiceLoader did NOT already work: the generic CollectionShadow iterator law claimed ServiceLoader receivers (hasNext=false via empty CollectionState). Fixed by (a) the S102 decline law in CollectionShadow::dispatch (receivers carrying the S102 'service' load-marker are declined) and (b) widening S102's iterator block to accept the ServiceLoader-typed runtime dispatch (class_name == Ljava/util/ServiceLoader;) and to re-stamp the __sld_service__ marker from the load-time `service` field. Positive AND negative semantics both verified after the fix.
section4_note: dooz v23 APK carries R8-renamed META-INF/services entries: 'e6' -> m6 (MainDispatcherFactory -> AndroidDispatcherFactory) and 'pr'. The S102 engine law reads META-INF/services/<name> from real APK entries, so renamed service contracts are handled by the same generic mechanism. Dispatchers.Main itself remains unreached on dooz (blocked earlier by F-NEW-253); the mechanism-level questions in directive section 4 are answered from this evidence without any Lv;.o-style interception.
